text.headline: The History of Machine Learning
text.text: Key milestones from the history of machine learning and artificial intelligence covered in lessons 1–2, from Bayes' theorem to recurrent neural networks.

text.headline: Machines that think and the golden years

media.caption: A geometric visualisation of Bayes' theorem.

text.headline: Bayes' theorem
text.text:
Thomas Bayes' essay on probability is published posthumously by Richard Price. Bayes' theorem later becomes a foundation for probabilistic inference.

Source: Wikipedia — Bayes' theorem

media.caption: Adrien-Marie Legendre.
media.credit: Julien-Léopold Boilly, Public domain, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: Least squares theory
text.text:
Adrien-Marie Legendre introduces the method of least squares, a technique for fitting a model to noisy data that is central to regression.

Source: Wikipedia — Least squares

media.caption: Andrey Markov.
media.credit: Unknown author, Public domain, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: Markov chains
text.text:
Andrey Markov introduces Markov chains, in which the next state depends only on the current state.

Source: Wikipedia — Markov chain

media.caption: Alan Turing, 1951.
media.credit: Elliott & Fry, Public domain, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: Turing proposes the imitation game
text.text:
Alan Turing publishes Computing Machinery and Intelligence, proposing the imitation game — later known as the Turing Test.

Source: Turing (1950)

media.caption: John McCarthy.
media.credit: "null0" via Flickr, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: Dartmouth Summer Research Project
text.text:
The Dartmouth Summer Research Project on artificial intelligence is held. John McCarthy and colleagues coin the term "artificial intelligence" for the proposal.

Source: Wikipedia — Dartmouth workshop

media.caption: Mark I Perceptron (operator's manual figure).
media.credit: U.S. Government, Public domain, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: Rosenblatt introduces the perceptron
text.text:
Frank Rosenblatt describes the perceptron, a trainable linear classifier that underlies early work on neural networks.

Source: Wikipedia — Perceptron

media.caption: A conversation with ELIZA.
media.credit: Joe Strout, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: ELIZA, an early chatterbot
text.text:
ELIZA, an early 'chatterbot', could converse with people and act as a primitive 'therapist'.

Source: Wikipedia — ELIZA

media.caption: Schematic view of k-nearest neighbors classification.

text.headline: Nearest Neighbor
text.text:
The nearest neighbor algorithm is used to map routes and, in ML contexts, to detect patterns.

Source: Wikipedia — k-nearest neighbors algorithm

media.caption: Diagram of a feedforward neural network.

text.headline: Backpropagation
text.text:
Backpropagation is used to train feedforward neural networks.

Source: Wikipedia — Backpropagation

text.headline: SHRDLU and the blocks world
text.text:
"Blocks world" was an example of a micro-world where blocks could be stacked and sorted. Experiments with SHRDLU helped propel language processing forward.

Source: Wikipedia — SHRDLU

media.caption: Shakey the robot.
media.credit: SRI International, Public domain, Wikimedia Commons

text.headline: Shakey the robot
text.text:
Shakey the robot could maneuver and decide how to perform tasks 'intelligently'.

Source: Wikipedia — Shakey the robot

text.headline: Recurrent Neural Networks
text.text:
Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are artificial neural networks derived from feedforward neural networks that create temporal graphs.

Source: Wikipedia — Recurrent neural network

text.headline: Smartphones and the rise of big data
text.text: The amount of data began to rapidly increase and become more widely available, especially with the advent of the smartphone around 2007

text.headline: ChatGPT and AI
text.text:
ChatGPT and AI are the latest advances in natural language processing.

Source: Wikipedia — ChatGPT
